title: Prompt telemetry hashing and sampling privacy guardrail
author: Liam Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This decision record defines a standardized contract for capturing, hashing, and sampling prompt telemetry across Redwood services to balance operational observability and user privacy. The contract prescribes a deterministic, privacy-aware fingerprinting algorithm, a tiered sampling policy, required telemetry fields, and allowed usages. The goal is to enable reliable debugging, quality monitoring, and regression detection while minimizing exposure of user content and meeting compliance requirements.

Motivation
----------
- Prompt contents are the most valuable signals for diagnosing model regressions, prompt drift, and for building quality guardrails.
- Raw prompts can contain PII, proprietary customer secrets, and regulatory data. Storing or routing raw prompt text broadly increases risk and compliance burden.
- Teams need consistent fingerprints to correlate requests across systems (inference logs, eval harness, alerting).
- A reproducible, privacy-focused fingerprint + sampling policy supports downstream analytics without centralizing raw prompts.

Scope
-----
This contract applies to all Redwood-hosted inference entrypoints (API, streaming, internal orchestration), Redwood Dedicated control plane telemetry, and the optional Private telemetry shim when customers opt in. It does NOT mandate private deployment customer data routing policy; it only defines the telemetry fields and algorithms used when telemetry leaves the compute boundary.

Decision
--------
1) Deterministic fingerprinting: services must derive a request_fingerprint for each prompt interaction using the algorithm below. The fingerprint must be stable for identical prompt inputs and deterministic across language runtimes. Services must NOT store raw prompt text alongside telemetry unless explicitly approved in a restricted store.

2) Privacy-preserving hash algorithm: implement HMAC-SHA256 with a per-cluster telemetry key (K_telemetry) and salt derived from model family and prompt-length-bucket. The final fingerprint is the hex-encoded first-64 bits of HMAC(K_telemetry, normalized_prompt || bucket_tag).

- Normalization: strip whitespace, convert to NFC unicode, remove deterministic meta tokens (timestamps, ephemeral ids) per normalization rules in Appendix A.
- Key management: K_telemetry is rotated quarterly and stored in KMS. Rotation must maintain the ability to resolve historic fingerprints for no more than 90 days; after 90 days, mapping is not guaranteed.

3) Tiered sampling policy: telemetry emission must follow a 3-tier sampling model to minimize downstream exposure and cost.

- Tier 0 (full): 100% of internal regression experiments and canary traffic. Raw prompt allowed in restricted diagnostic stores only with explicit approver and audit.
- Tier 1 (fingerprint + metadata): 100% of production requests emit fingerprint, model id, token counts, top-level request metadata (tenant, region), latency buckets, and top-level error codes. No raw prompt text.
- Tier 2 (sampled raw): 1% by default of production traffic emits raw normalized prompt text in addition to fingerprint; sample rate configurable per customer and per model. Sampled raw prompts must be stored in a restricted bucket with retention <= 90 days.

4) Observability schema: telemetry events must include the following fields (all services):
- request_fingerprint (string),
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601),
- model_family (string),
- model_version (string),
- tenant_id (string, hashed id when required by policy),
- prompt_tokens (int),
- response_tokens (int),
- latency_ms (int),
- error_class (string|null),
- sampling_tier (string: tier0|tier1|tier2),
- telemetry_version (string),
- prompt_source_tag (string: api|batch|canary|internal).

5) SLI and alerting hooks: correlation keys for SLO investigations must use request_fingerprint and telemetry_version. Alerts that surface prompt-level signals (e.g., sudden rise in hallucination rate for a fingerprint cluster) should reference fingerprint clusters and only include raw sample prompts when running in a diagnostics session.

6) Access controls and storage: any storage that contains raw prompts (Tier 0 or sampled Tier 2) must be labeled restricted, have RBAC limited to diagnostic engineers and security, be encrypted-at-rest with KMS keys, and have an automated retention purge set to 90 days or less. Fingerprint-only telemetry can be stored longer (default 2 years) for longitudinal analysis.

7) Telemetry contract versioning: telemetry_version is a required field. Any incompatible change to fingerprint algorithm, normalization rules, or sampling semantics must create a new telemetry_version and trigger a migration plan with a roll-forward testing window.

Implementation details
----------------------
- Language SDKs must provide a small reference library (python/node/go) that implements normalization and HMAC-SHA256 fingerprint derivation to ensure consistency. The library must expose: compute_fingerprint(normalized_prompt, model_family, bucket_tag) -> string.
- Bucket tagging rules: prompt length buckets are: tiny (<=32 tokens), short (33-128), medium (129-512), long (>512). The bucket_tag is model_family + ":" + bucket_name.
- Example fingerprint pseudo-code: H = HMAC_SHA256(K, "v1|" + model_family + "|" + bucket + "|" + normalized_prompt); fingerprint = hex(H)[:16];
- Telemetry sinks: prefix fingerprint-only events with telemetry_version and use a different kafka topic (telemetry.fp.v{n}) from raw-sampled topic (telemetry.raw.v{n}) to simplify access controls.

Operational playbook (rollout and incident steps)
------------------------------------------------
1) Library rollout: land reference SDK in canary services and run side-by-side validation for 2 weeks comparing existing telemetry with fingerprint collisions observed.
2) Canary: enable fingerprint-only emission for 5% of production traffic for 1 week, verify latencies and upstream pipeline throughput at +10% load margin.
3) Sampling config: enable Tier 2 sampling at 0.1% initially; escalate to 1% if diagnostic coverage insufficient.
4) Incident handling: if a fingerprint collision cluster is suspected (collision rate > 0.01% of requests for same fingerprint and different normalized prompts), label event and trigger differential debugging with full raw capture for affected canary nodes only.

SLOs and metrics to track
-------------------------
- fingerprint_collision_rate <= 0.001% per model_family (monthly).
- telemetry_ingest_failure_rate <= 0.05% (5xx/failures to telemetry sinks).
- sampling_pii_detection_rate <= 0.01% (rate where sampled raw prompts contain high-risk PII after normalization).

Appendix A: Normalization rules (summary)
----------------------------------------
- Trim leading/trailing whitespace and collapse repeated whitespace to single spaces.
- Unicode normalize to NFC.
- Remove deterministic ISO8601 timestamps using regex patterns.
- Replace sequences that match common auth tokens or key patterns with <REDACTED_TOKEN> placeholder.
- Keep structural tokens and annotations (function calls, tool names) since they are important for behavior analysis.

Security and compliance considerations
-------------------------------------
- KMS-managed telemetry keys reduce risk of raw prompt leakage across environments. Rotations are audited.
- Retention windows align with our compliance baseline and can be shortened for higher-risk customers.
- Customers with explicit regulatory restrictions may opt out of Tier 2 sampling; telemetry will default to fingerprint-only.

Ownership and follow-ups
-----------------------
- Owner: Observability Platform team (observability@redwood.internal).
- Implementers: SDKs (dx-sdk), Runtime logging pipeline, Canary infra.
- Required follow-ups: publish SDKs, add automated tests to verify fingerprint stability, and add a telemetry_version migration runbook.

FAQ
---
Q: Why not use plain SHA256 without HMAC?
A: HMAC with a cluster key prevents adversaries from computing fingerprints if they obtain prompt examples; it also enables controlled key rotation.

Q: How are customer privacy requests handled?
A: Data subject requests are handled by the security/legal process. When a customer requests deletion, the mapping between fingerprint and any sampled raw prompt must be revoked and corresponding stored samples purged.
